questions.question: One radian is approximately equal to:
questions.explanation: One radian equals 180/pi degrees ≈ 57.3 degrees.

questions.question: The angle subtended at the center of a circle by an arc equal to its radius is:

A radian is the angle formed when arc length equals radius.
θ = s/r = r/r = 1 radian.

questions.question: The SI unit of angular velocity is:

questions.question: If a body completes one revolution in 2 seconds, its angular velocity is:
questions.explanation: ω = total angle / time = 2π / 2 = π rad/s.

questions.question: Angular acceleration is defined as the rate of change of:
questions.explanation: Angular acceleration is change in angular velocity per unit time.

questions.question: The relationship between linear velocity (v) and angular velocity (ω) is:

questions.question: A body moving in a circle has constant angular velocity. Its tangential acceleration is:

Tangential acceleration = r × angular acceleration. If angular velocity is constant, acceleration is

questions.question: The acceleration directed towards the center of a circle is:
questions.explanation: Centripetal acceleration always points toward the center.

questions.question: The force required to keep a body moving in a circle is:
questions.explanation: Centripetal force is the net inward force keeping circular motion.

questions.question: If speed is doubled, centripetal force becomes:
questions.explanation: Centripetal force depends on v², so doubling speed makes force four times larger.
